caseno: First Miscellaneous Appeal No. 697 of 1991 with connected Civil Rule No.416 (FM)/1991
lawyer:
Mr. Md. Mozaffar Hossain with Mr. Md. Abdur Rahim. Advocate ------ For the appellant.
Mr. Md. Fazlul Karim with Mr. Zahedul Bari. Advocates ------ For respondent No. 1.
parties:
Imtiaj Ali ------ Appellant.
Vs.
Eskander Mirja ------ Respondent.
full_judgment:
Mr. Mahmudul Amin Chowdhury, J:-This appeal is by the defendant-appellant against the order of rejection of Miscellaneous Case No. 13 of 1987 filed under Order 9. Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure. 

 2. The short fact leading to this miscellaneous case is that the respondent instituted other Class Suit No. 46 of 1986 in the Court of the learned Subordinate Judge, Bogra against the present appellant and another for specific performance of Contract. That suit was ultimately decreed ex parte. Thereafter the present appellant filed Miscellaneous Case No. 13 of 1987 under Order 9, Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure and prayed for setting aside the ex parte decree on the ground that summons of the suit were not served upon any of the defendants rather the same was suppressed. 

 3. In the miscellaneous case the plain-tiff-respondent entered appearance and filed a written objection denying the allegations contending inter alia that sum- 1 months of the original Other Class Suit No. 46 of 1986 were duly served upon the defendants including the present appellant who was hold for statutory attorney. It is their further case that summons of the suit were also served by registered post and since there was nothing to cons test the suit. The defendants in spite of service of summons failed to appear on the date fixed. Consequently the suit was.' decreed ex parte and the decree was ultimately executed in O.0 Execution Case No. 6 of 1986 and another O.C. Execution Case No. 11 of 1986 is pending which was filed for recovery of the costs. 

 4. Before the trial Court both the parties adduced oral and documentary evidence in support of their respective cases. The learned Subordinate Judge then by his judgment dated 26.8.91 dismissed the miscellaneous case and refused to set aside the ex parte decree. The defendant No 1 of the original suit then preferred this appeal before this Court. 

 5. Mr. Mozaffar Hossain along with Mr. M.A. Rahim, the learned Advocates appeared on behalf of the appellant and they submitted that the summons upon the defendants have not been served rather those are suppressed even there was no service of summons by registered post as required under the law and by suppressing the summons the plaintiff secured the ex parte decree. It has been contended that the decree was obtained in haste will be evident from the fact that the suit was filed on 29.1.86 and the ex parte decree was obtained on 13.3.86 and this haste indicate that fraud was practiced upon the Court by the plaintiff in securing the decree. The learned Advocate contends that by misleading the Court the present ex parte decree has been obtained. The learned Advocate further submits that if the evidence adduced from the side of the opposite party-respondents adduced in the miscellaneous case is considered it will appear that there was no service of summons. 

 6. Mr. Md. Fazlul Karim, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the plain-tiff-respondents on the other hand submits that the evidence of O.P. Ws. 2 and 3 coupled with the service return proved that when the defendants refused to accept the summons those are served by hanging which were accepted by the trial Court as sufficient service and as such there was no suppression of summons. He further submitted that when the constituted attorney refused to accept the summons it may be construed as proper ser-vice and that has been done in the original suit, that the learned Advocate further contends that the miscellaneous case was filed not by the petitioner herself but through her constituted attorney and then as the power of attorney that was submit-ted before the court was not revalided in this country that cannot be considered and as such it may be construed that the miscellaneous case was not filed by the present appellant herself and some other interested persons are working behind the scene. 

 7. The respondent instituted O.C. Suit No. 46 of 1986 before the learned Subordinate Judge, Bogra for Specific Performance of Contract and his case is that he entered into a contract with the present appellant for purchase of the suit property at a consideration of Tk. 16,25,000.00 and he was inducted into possession when the entire consideration money was paid and there was a stipulation that on obtaining income tax clearance certificate the kabala would be executed. But as the appellant failed to exe-cute and register the kabala the plaintiff had instituted the suit for Specific Performance of Contract. 

 8. The present miscellaneous case has been filed on the ground of obtaining the ex parte decree in the original suit on suppression of the summons. The respondent raised an objection that the power of attorney which was produced before the trial Court and the attorney who was instrumental in filling the miscellaneous case has not been revalidated in this country and no one can act on the basis of that power of attorney and from that the learned Advocate for the respondent tried to impress that the miscellaneous case cannot be maintained. It appears from the impugned judgment that the power of attorney Ext. 6 is a product of fraud and forgery and the petitioner never executed it, and therefore, P.W. 1 is neither attorney nor a Karjakarak of the appellant. The trial Court it appears took great pain in discarding the power of attorney and after discarding the same came to the finding that the present case has not been filed by the appellant. But it is well settled that when the Court finds that the power of attorney is bad, the only order that the Court can pass is under Order HI, Rule 4(1). The Court shall debar the Advocate to act for the party in the Court, for the simple reason that he has not been appointed for the purpose by or under a valid power of attorney and has therefore, no authority to act on behalf of the party in the Court. The disability attaches to the Advocate and not to the plaint. In such circumstances the court will next sit a date for steps to be taken by the plaintiff and on the next date several options are open to the plaintiff. He may appear in person or by another recognised agent or by the same recognised agent after removing the objections that have been taken with regard to the validity of the power of attorney. It has been held in the case of Anath Bandhu Guha & Sons Ltd., through its attorney Md. Sirajul Huq Vs. Babu Sudhangshu Shekhar Haider, reported in 42 D.L.R. (AD) 244, that when the power of attorney fails the embargo that follows will fall upon the Advocate and not on prosecution of the suit by the principal. This disability attaches to the Advocate not to the plaint. 

 9. It appears from the record that the trial Court on the face of objection from the present respondents directed for the personal appearance of the petitioner, but thereafter the petitioner produced a power of attorney which was not accepted as valid and correct power of attorney by the trial Court. But in such circumstances the trial Court ought to have direct for further correct and better power of attorney but instead of doing that the Court proceeded with the disposal of the miscellaneous case. The Court found that the power of attorney is forged and fabricated. May be it was forged and fabricated but that can-not be a ground for dismissal of the miscellaneous case in view of the aforesaid decision of our Appellate Division. 

 12. The second part is that after the insertion of the rule 19A and 19B of Order V of the Code of Civil Procedure, it appears that when a suit is filed the Court shall, in addition to, and simultaneously with, the issue of summons for service in the manner provided in rules 9 to 19 (both inclusive), also direct the summons to be served by registered post with acknowledgement due addressed to the defendant or his agent empowered to accept the service at the place where the defendant or his agent actually and voluntarily resides and carries on business or personally works for gain. It is the definite case of the respondent that the summons were sent to defendant No. 1 to be served on his constituted attorney defendant No. 5. We have carefully gone through the records of the trial court but we are not find anything to show that this provision of Rule 19B of the Code of Civil Procedure has been complied with. The order sheet is very much silent and even in the record there is no material and we find that actually there was sending of the summons by registered post with acknowledgement due. There is nothing on record to indicate that the postal acknowledgement due was received by the trial court and no step was taken in the miscellaneous case by the respondent to examine the postal peon to prove the service of summons sent by registered post with A/D. It has also been provided in sub-rule (2) of Rule 19B of Order V of the Code of Civil Procedure that where the summons were properly addressed pre-paid and duly sent by registered post with acknowledgement due, the declaration referred to in this sub-rule may be made notwithstanding the fact that the acknowledgement having been lost or mislaid or for any other reason, has not been received by the court within thirty days from the date of issue of the summons. This indicate that the Court is required to wait for thirty days from issuance of summons be put for proceeding further which is very much absent in the present case before us. The suit was filed on 29.1.86 and it appears that on the same date summons were handed over to the process server who served the same on 7.6.86 and the suit was decreed on 13.3.86. This fact indicate that there was no compliance of this proviso of sub-rule (2) of Rule 19B of Order 5 of the Code of Civil Procedure. All these it appears that has escaped the notice of the trial Court while disposing of the suit ex parte. 

 13. Now, from a consideration of the materials on record it appears that by suppressing the summons sent through official process and by not complying with the provision of Rule 19B of Order V of the Code of Civil Procedure the ex parte decree has been obtained. It has been held by our Appellate Division in the case of Abul Khair Mia Vs. Abdul Latif Sardar, reported in XXXII D.L.R. (AD) 167, that the ex parte decree obtained by suppressing of summons is a decree obtained fraudulently. Such a decree obtained fraudulently is a nullity. In view of our finding that the decree has been obtained by suppressing of summons and by misleading the Court following the aforesaid decision of our Appellate Division we hold that this decree has been questioned in the miscellaneous case is a nullity. 

 15. The learned Advocate for the respondents submits that the case was not filed within statutory period of time. -- The same was according to him barred by limitation. In 34 D.L.R's. case of our Appellate Division it has been held that when a fraud is proved then there is question of limitation. This will run from the date when the fraud is detected. Here in the present case before us the fraud was proved at the time of disposal of the case 'by the trial Court. So, the question of limitation does not arise. 

 16. Furthermore, even if it is found that the fraud was detected earlier a Court is not debarred of any power to interfere in the matter when practice of fraud upon the party as well as upon the Court is detected the civil court can act under Section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure. It has been held in the case of Mofazzal Molla & another Vs. Parul Bala Debi & Ors., reported in 24 D.L.R. 78, that as to cases where fraud is committed upon the Court as well as upon the parties, a Court has inherent jurisdiction to interfere in the matter in exercising of its power vested in Section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure. The same view has been expressed in the case of Mozaffar Ahmed & Ors. Vs. Moulvi Saleh Ahmed & Ors, reported in XL D.L.R 239, in the case of Md. Amir Hossain Sarder Vs. Sarat Chandra & Ors. reported In XXXI D.L.R. 109 and in the case of Master Abdul Aziz Vs. Abani Mohan Mukherjee and others, reported in XXX D.L.R. (AD) 221. So, this is the consistent view of the higher Court of this Country that when the fraud is detected and committed either upon the parties or upon the Court is a sufficient ground for civil Court to invoke the provision of Section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure. Here in this case we have already found that a fraud has been com-mitted on the defendant-appellants as well as upon the Court and as such this court can exercise the jurisdiction conferred under Section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure in setting aside the ex parte decree. 

 17. Mr. Md. Fazlul Karim, the learned Advocate for the respondent No. 1 also questioned the propriety of taking into evidence the power of attorney on the ground that this was duly stamped in this country or revalided as per law. So this document cannot be considered. But it is the consistent view of the higher court of this country that once a document is admitted into evidence its admissibility cannot be questioned in any court at any stage of the same suit on the ground of insufficiency of stamp. In the present case it appears that the power of attorney was taken into evidence without any objection. Now at this stage the respondent was not allowed to raise question on its admissibility. The earnest decision came to our notice on this point in the case of Amin Jute Being Co. Ltd. Vs. Aminpur Union Co-operative Multi-purpose Society Ltd., reported in XII D.L.R. 590. Where it has been held that section 35 of the Stamp Act prohibit a Court from admitting in evidence an instrument which in its view is not duly stamped. This section also prohibits the Court from acting on such document. If the Court however wrongly admits such a document, the appellate Court is prevented by Section 36 of the Stamp Act from calling in question the admission in evidence of such (an Instrument), though it may have been wrongly admitted. This view has been followed in the case of Abul Hashem Vs. Serajul Haque and others, reported in 13 D.L.R. 16 and also in the case of M/s. Boulat Ltd. Vs. Pubali Bank, reported in 39 D.L.R 243. In view of the consistent decisions of the higher court of this Country we hold that the admissibility of the power of attorney cannot now be re-opened at this stage in this Court. 

 18. Mr. Md. Fazlul Karim also raised in question on the Notarial Act done on the power of attorney. It appears that the power of attorney was notarised by the Notary Public at Peshwar, Pakistan, but before the trial Court nothing has been produced to show that the person who notarised the document has not appointed by the Government of Pakistan as a Notary Public. Mere submission by the learned Advocate will be of no help with-out any material to hold that the person who signed one document as notary public was not appointed as such. It has been held in the case of Nurunnessa and others Vs. Babar Ali Bepari reported in 33 D.L.R. (AD) 124. that notarial acts done by foreign country can be accepted in Bangladesh provided the person before 

 whom the notarial act was done as a notary public and the state authorised him to do the notarial act. Here in this present case before us the power of attorney was notarised by notary public at 

 19. In this matter a further question was raised that the power of attorney was not revalidated in this country. The revalidation was done in the Stamp Acts, if the document is found to be not properly stamped the party concerned get it revalidated or get it properly stamped or the Court itself may impound the document but insufficiency of stamp cannot be a ground to discard a document already taken into evidence. In the 39 D.L.R's case it has been held that the admissibility of such a document cannot be questioned in any Court at any stage of the same suit on the ground of insufficiency of stamp. In view of this decision we find little substance in the submission made by Mr. Karim. 

 22. In view of the aforesaid we hold that this is a fit case where this Court should interfere and set aside the impugned judgment and allow the Miscellaneous Appeal and restored the original suit to its file and number. 

 23. The appeal is allowed. The judgment and order dated 26.8.1991 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, Bogra in Miscellaneous Case No 13 of 1987 is hereby set aside and the said case is hereby allowed and the judgment and decree passed in original O.C. Suit No. 46 of 1986 is hereby set aside and the same is restored to its original fine and number.
